jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in MRI radiofrequency detector development - DTU Space
jobs.description:
If you are passionate about advanced MRI technology and want to contribute to the next generation of medical imaging, this PhD position offers a unique opportunity to work at the forefront of radiofrequency detector development in collaboration with leading international researchers in Denmark and Australia.

A typical MRI scanner uses radiofrequency detectors to image water molecules. Imaging other molecules and nuclei requires additional new detectors and antennas. The objective of the PhD project is to demonstrate MR imaging of nuclei other than hydrogen by building MRI detectors and antennas, which can cover frequencies of multiple nuclei.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The main outcome of the project will be a broadband/multinuclear detector array, ready to be implemented in clinical environment. It is a cross-disciplinary project and collaboration with the Department of Health Technology at DTU as well as other national and international institutions, such as University of Queensland, Aarhus University Hospital, GE Healthcare, DRCMR and others is an essential part. 

The tasks and responsibilities include:

• Literature study and evaluation of different multi-frequency detector configurations and identifying the most promising;
• Develop efficient element decoupling strategies minimizing noise correlation between array elements;
• Design and implement multinuclear multichannel radiofrequency coil array for MRI;
• Imaging experiments:
• Coordinate efforts on mechanical and electrical safety tests end approval for clinical use;
• Disseminate the project results to the public and exchange of knowledge with society.
The applicant will take part in research-based teaching. 

Contributing to the development of a good work atmosphere and a thriving environment is essential.

The candidate should have a master’s degree in engineering, preferably in electrical engineering.

It is an advantage to have experience in

• High frequency circuit design, fabrication and testing;
• Use of VNAs, spectrum analysers, noise figure meters and other measurement equipment in circuit testing;
• High frequency circuit design software;
• MR technology.
The position also requires, that: 

• You are driven by pushing boundaries;
• You are motivated by both individual and team accomplishments;
• You thrive on collaboration and teamwork.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be conducted continuously.

DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures 

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date will be as soon as possible by mutual agreement with the candidate.

The primary workplace is at DTU Lyngby Campus and a longer stay of about 6 month is anticipated at University of Queensland, Australia.

jobs.description:
We offer PhD scholarships at DTU Compute to develop machine learning methods for faster analysis and optimization of cyber-physical systems. You will build predictive models of expensive analytical calculations and simulations, and use AI to find good solutions to optimization problems that cannot be solved exactly within practical computing budgets. 

You will join the Embedded Systems Engineering section and work with Prof. Paul Pop. The application areas are related to, e.g., software-defined vehicles, datacenters, industrial automation, and energy systems.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your research will connect learned prediction models with optimization methods. The PhD topics will be defined with the supervisors. You will:

• Develop surrogate models that predict results of complex analyses and simulations, such as execution delays, energy use, and resource demands.
• Use machine learning to guide configuration, scheduling, and resource allocation, reducing the need for expensive model evaluations.
• Evaluate solution quality, computing time, uncertainty, and transfer to new systems; check proposed solutions against the original models and constraints.
• Publish your research, collaborate with project partners, and contribute to teaching and student supervision.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Ideally, you have both a BSc and an MSc in machine learning or artificial intelligence. Degrees in computer science, applied mathematics, electrical engineering, or related fields with substantial ML/AI coursework and projects are also relevant.

You should have a strong foundation in machine learning, algorithms, probability, and linear algebra; experience implementing and evaluating models in Python; and good written and spoken English. Experience with optimization, reinforcement learning, or simulation is an advantage. Prior expertise in all application areas is not required.

Approval and Enrolment

The Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, Denmark, is offering a postdoctoral position in computational genomics, starting 01-02-2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position will be available for a 2,5-year period.

You will be part of a research environment focusing on computational genomics, bioinformatics, and AI-driven plant research. You will be contributing specifically to the area of development of computational methods that integrate pangenomic information and large language model (LLM)-based approaches and the focus of your position will be targeted long-read sequencing and high-resolution gene-space assembly in complex plant genomes. You will work experimentally with genomic datasets, develop and evaluate LLM-based methods, and validate sequencing workflows and gene-space assembly quality.

We expect that you will be an important part of the research environment and that you will contribute positively to the social working environment. We also expect that you will take part in our teaching activities and that you will report research results in high-impact scientific journals.

Your profile

We are searching for a highly motivated candidate who has

• A PhD in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a closely related discipline, with a deep focus on plant genomics, computational plant biology, or AI applications in plant science .

• Documented experience in computational genomics, bioinformatics, pangenomic data analysis, machine learning, deep learning, or LLM-based model development.

• Collaborative skills and ability to contribute effectively in teams. A fondness of taking the initiative and the motivation to pursue a scientific career.

Additional qualifications

Further, we will prefer candidates with some of the following qualifications:

• Experience with Oxford Nanopore sequencing or other long-read sequencing platforms.

• Experience in LLM-based model development, including model training, fine-tuning, or evaluation.

• Experience developing computational methods or software for genomic sequence analysis.

• Experience with high-performance computing, algorithm optimization, or large-scale genomic datasets

• Familiarity with pangenomic analysis, structural variation, or genome assembly

• Teaching and supervision experience at the BSc and MSc level

• Interest and experience in developing effective national and international research applications

Who we are

At the Department of Agroecology, our main goal is to contribute to sustainable solutions to some of the world’s biggest problems within the areas of soil, plants, animals, humans, and the environment. We want to make a difference by contributing to both fundamental knowledge generation and the attainment of sustainable production systems via innovative research, contracted policy advice, and education. We offer professional laboratories, greenhouses, semi-field, and field-scale research facilities, advanced computing capacities as well as an extensive national and international researcher network. The department consists of nine research sections with around 350 highly skilled employees, of which approximately 50% are scientific staff. More information can be found here.

We believe in encouraging inclusion, acceptance, and understanding by employing staff who bring unique perspectives to our department.

What we offer

jobs.description:
A postdoc position focusing on statistical genetic and the modelling of quantitative and disease resistance traits in commercial crops is available in March 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter at the Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG), Aarhus University.

The position

The postdoc will develop statistical models and methods in a new breeding program for cultivar mixtures primarily in wheat, supporting higher yield stability and disease resistance for sustainable wheat production.

Special focus will be on using genomic prediction for more efficient selection of new wheat lines and with special focus on prediction of the performance in cultivar mixtures specific combining ability between lines which raises interesting questions regarding experimental design and associated information of variation in the soil microbiome. This involves estimation of variance component models including microbiome and host relations to handle the genotype by environment interactions for traits recorded under different locations and environment conditions. Additionally, information of both genotyped and non-genotyped individuals need to be combined. Methods for evaluation and comparison of models should be developed and implemented in breeding schemes that involve traditional monoline information as well as phenotypic information from populations of mixtures. The postdoc is expected to pursue internationally recognized research in computational methods for genetic evaluation such as linear mixed models, hierarchical models with random effects. We in particular welcome applicants with interest in method development for large scale genetic evaluation using dense genomic information. The position is for 2 years of employment and there are possibilities for extension up to a maximum of 4 years if the candidate is considered qualified and sufficient funding is available. The position is related to collaborative projects together with commercial breeding companies with the goal of developing methods and models that can be implemented in commercial breeding programs. The position provides excellent possibilities for access to state-of-the-art tools for simulation and for the analysis of complex genomic datasets, writing publications, and collaboration with industry partners as well as with other national and international research groups.

jobs.occupation: One or more PhD Stipends in Direct Air Capture Technologies
jobs.description:
The future of climate action extends beyond reducing emissions
Atmospheric CO2 concentrations continue to rise despite global efforts to reduce emissions. Achieving climate neutrality will therefore require not only deep emission reductions but also large-scale carbon removal solutions. Direct Air Capture (DAC) is one of the few technologies capable of permanently removing CO2 directly from the atmosphere, but significant scientific and engineering challenges remain before DAC can be deployed at gigaton scale. Future DAC systems must be energy-efficient, economically viable, and designed around a fundamental understanding of how materials, processes, and system integration interact.

At Aalborg University, we are seeking ambitious PhD candidates who want to help develop the next generation of DAC technologies through advanced process modelling, experimental studies, and techno-economic evaluations.

The stipend is open for appointment from 1 January 2027 or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years.

In the future, removing CO2 from the atmosphere will become an essential part of climate action.
Atmospheric CO2 is already changing the climate. Reducing emissions is essential, but it may not be enough. We must also learn how to remove carbon already present in the atmosphere. Future Direct Air Capture systems will not simply capture CO2:

They will integrate with renewable energy systems. They will operate flexibly and balance the energy systems. They will become scalable climate infrastructure.

What this PhD is really about
The stipends are designed to contribute to two ambitious research initiatives that aim to accelerate the development of Direct Air Capture technologies:

Development of process-aware methodologies for evaluating emerging DAC liquid and solid sorbents and technologies. Development of predictive frameworks linking sorbent properties to process-level DAC performance.

Together, these efforts seek to establish the scientific foundations required to move DAC development from empirical trial-and-error toward predictive, data-driven design and scale-up.

The research environment and culture you will step into
You will join CarbonLab at Aalborg University, a growing research environment dedicated to carbon capture, carbon removal, and climate-positive technologies. We are a group of approximately 20 people currently represented by 7 different nationalities. Our research combines laboratory experiments, process modelling, experimental validation, techno-economic and LCA assessments, and system integration to accelerate the deployment of DAC solutions at scale.

At CarbonLab, we are building more than technologies; we are building a research community. Our researchers share ideas openly, collaborate across disciplines, and celebrate each other's successes. PhD students are treated as colleagues, encouraged to develop their own scientific identity, and supported in taking initiative from the very beginning. Whether presenting at international conferences, contributing to teaching, leading collaborations, or exploring new research directions, you will be part of a culture that combines scientific ambition with mutual trust and genuine support. We believe that excellent research and an excellent research environment go hand in hand.

Your research qualifications
We are looking for highly motivated candidates who are passionate about addressing climate change through scientific research and technological innovation. The ideal candidate has a strong analytical mindset, enjoys solving complex engineering challenges, and is eager to contribute to the development of next-generation carbon removal technologies.

You should hold a master's degree (or be close to completion) in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Energy Engineering, Chemistry, Physics, or a related discipline.

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage:

Direct Air Capture, carbon capture, or carbon removal technologies Chemical process engineering and process intensification Mass transfer, reaction engineering, and thermodynamics Experimental design and laboratory testing Spectroscopy and related analytical techniques such as Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR). Measurement and interpretation of gas-liquid and gas-solid equilibrium data and breakthrough experiments. Process modelling and simulation (e.g., Aspen Plus, MATLAB, Python, or similar tools) Data analysis, optimization, and uncertainty assessment Techno-economic analysis and sustainability assessment Energy systems integration and renewable energy technologies

In addition, we value candidates who:

Demonstrate scientific curiosity and creativity Take initiative and ownership of their research Enjoy working both independently and collaboratively Communicate scientific results effectively in written and spoken English Thrive in an interdisciplinary and international research environment Are motivated to contribute to solutions with real-world climate impact

Previous research experience through master's projects, internships, conference contributions, or scientific publications is considered an advantage but is not a formal requirement.

Qualification requirements
PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

AAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners and other academic environments to address real-world energy challenges. The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and from a broad range of national backgrounds. This creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as the working language in research and teaching, which makes it straightforward for international colleagues to integrate. We offer access to advanced laboratories and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday life. New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters. You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk

Would you like to help support research and development in a supportive and collaborative environment?
The Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University is seeking a new employee for running lab-scale experiments with intact soil cores to assess the effect of different fertilizers and supplements, such as rock flour, on soil gaseous nitrogen losses and soil nitrogen leaching, with a starting date of 1st March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is available for a fixed term of 18 months.

The position is based on a 37-hour work week. Depending on the nature of the role and its responsibilities, periods of high workload may occur, during which overtime should be expected.

You will become part of Land-CRAFT, where you will work closely with researchers, technical and administrative colleagues, and, where relevant, students. The position is directly linked to two ongoing GUDP projects: RockFlour and Opti-BioN, and it offers an opportunity to contribute to the department’s core activities and daily operations within an active and engaging research environment.

Your tasks
• Designing and running soil core experiments
• Measuring the soil physical and chemical properties, calculating greenhouse gas fluxes, processing and interpreting data 
• Project management tasks, including communicating with the project partners and organizing meetings
• Preparing reports to funders and contributing to grant applications with data, plots, analyses and writing
Your profile

We expect that
• You have an MSc in Agricultural, Environmental, Soil Sciences, or similar
• You can demonstrate a minimum of two years' experience in designing and running soil experiments targeting greenhouse gas (GHG) balances and nitrogen (N) leaching.
• You have experience of measuring the soil properties and calculating greenhouse gas fluxe
• You have good English skills, and you thrive in an inclusive multi-cultural and diverse working environment
• You are motivated by working on projects, where the overall aim is to support the green transition in agriculture

Who we are
 At the Department of Agroecology, our main goal is to contribute to sustainable solutions to some of the world’s biggest problems within the areas of soil, plants, animals, humans, and the environment. We want to make a difference by contributing to both fundamental knowledge generation and the attainment of sustainable production systems via innovative research, contracted policy advice, and education. We offer professional laboratories, greenhouses, semi-field, and field-scale research facilities, advanced computing capacities as well as an extensive national and international researcher network. The department consists of nine research sections with around 350 highly skilled employees, of which approximately 50% are scientific staff. More information can be found here.

We believe in encouraging inclusion, acceptance, and understanding by employing staff who bring unique perspectives to our department.

What we offer
• A collaborative, international research environment that combines high academic standards with an informal and supportive atmosphere. We value accountability, curiosity, flexibility, and teamwork in everything we do.
• An inclusive and respectful workplace culture, where mutual trust, kindness, and professional dialogue are part of daily life. We encourage open communication and develop a cohesive sense of community across teams and disciplines.
• A flexible working environment that supports work-life balance and individual needs.
• An active institutional commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion – in recruitment, career development, and everyday interactions.
• An innovative and meaningful workplace where your work contributes to solving real-world challenges. No two days are alike, and we welcome creative thinking and new ideas.
• Support for international researchers and their families, including Relocation Service and an Expat Partner Programme
Living and working in Denmark
• Subsidised childcare and free education from primary school through university.
• Universal healthcare for you and your family as residents.
• Five weeks of paid holiday per year.
• Generous parental leave – up to 52 weeks shared between parents, with full or partial salary.
Place of Work
The place of work Ole Worms Alle 3, Department of Agroecology, Faculty of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University.

Contact
Applicants seeking further information can contact Professor Klaus Butterbach-Bahl (e-mail: klaus.butterbach-bahl@agro.au.dk)

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 24 November 2026. 

Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion.
